title: Module quiz: MCP in Claude Code

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A team's shared `.mcp.json` starts a documentation server with the argument `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/tools/docs_server.py`, and on every machine the server fails to start with that text unexpanded in the path. What should the entry say?

options.text: The name moved into the `env` map so that the process receives it
options.says: Ruled out because the text in `args` would still have nothing to expand from: "so `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project file has nothing to expand from".

options.text: An absolute location from the lead developer's own checkout, fixed for all
options.says: Ruled out because a personal location fails on every other machine: "A value that is not secret, such as a base URL or a path, should have a default".

options.text: The same line placed in the user-level file, where the name is set
options.says: Ruled out because moving the entry does not give the variable a value in Claude Code's own environment, and the documented answer is a default: "The documentation's answer is a default such as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}`".

options.text: A fallback after the name, written with a colon and a dash
options.says: The variable is set for the server and not for Claude Code, so a path in `command` or `args` needs a fallback.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A CI job runs `claude -p` on a fresh clone, and a pull request has added a server to `.mcp.json` that nobody on the team has seen. What happens when the job starts?

options.text: It stays pending until a person approves it in an interactive session
options.says: Ruled out because the prompt needs a person: "In `claude -p` runs, Agent SDK sessions, and cloud sessions, Claude Code can't show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking."

options.text: It is skipped, and the job runs without that server
options.says: Ruled out by the same sentence, which says such a run loads project-scoped servers and does not skip them: "it loads project-scoped servers without asking".

options.text: It loads without asking and is available in that run
options.says: Unattended runs cannot show the approval prompt.

options.text: It loads only if the repository's own settings file approves it in advance
options.says: Ruled out because "approvals committed to the project's `.claude/settings.json` are ignored in a folder you have not trusted".

questions.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent's backend tools come from twelve MCP servers listed in the shared file, and sessions start with crowded context. A developer reads that tools from all servers are available simultaneously and marks all twelve servers `alwaysLoad`. What is the effect?

options.text: Startup waits without limit for the servers to connect
options.says: Ruled out because the wait is bounded: "capped at the standard 5-second connect timeout".

options.text: All their definitions return to the prompt at launch, undoing deferral
options.says: `alwaysLoad` brings every definition into the initial context.

options.text: Only the tools that the first request needs are loaded, the rest later
options.says: Ruled out because loading only what a request needs is what tool search does, and the flag turns that off: "Putting it on every server defeats tool search."

options.text: Each tool gets the name of its server added so that names stay unique
options.says: Ruled out because naming already carries the server: "a tool is called `mcp__<server>__<tool>`".

origin.section: All servers, one set of tools
